record.label: One measured configuration approaches its instance maximum
record.statement: For each epsilon>0 there is one finite deterministic cost/mixer word W, independent of n and disorder J, such that Pr_{J,Sigma}[H_n,J(Sigma)>=max_sigma H_n,J(sigma)-epsilon*n] tends to one. Sigma is one computational-basis measurement from W. The union bound combines measured-energy and maximum concentration for the same disorder without independence. No every-instance guarantee, effective threshold, variable-depth theorem or efficient angle selection is supplied.
record.boundary: Ordinary authored deduction checked against retained mathematical inputs; no new Lean declaration, elaborated dependency, cross-model transport, Comparator acceptance or independent proof certification is asserted.

The convergence $\mathbb E M_n\to P_*$ makes its bias at most $\varepsilon/4$ for all sufficiently large $n$. ### 5.3 A fixed QAOA circuit before the thermodynamic limit The remaining consequence uses a separate circuit approximation theorem, stated as Proposition 5 below. We give its finite Gaussian input and identify the energy it approximates. Its operator and control construction is developed in the companion; the support and density proofs above do not require those additional prerequisites. Let $\widehat Z_i,\widehat X_i$ be Pauli operators, and define the cost and mixer by $$ C_{n,J}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i0$ there is one finite $W$ with $v(W)\geq P_*-\varepsilon$, whose depth and angles depend on $\varepsilon$ but not on $n$ or $J$. The instance still determines $C_{n,J}$. Here depth counts global cost–mixer layers; their elementary gate counts depend on the implementation. This order of limits differs from the fixed-instance depth limit in [Farhi, Goldstone and Gutmann, §VI][FGG], which permits instance-dependent choices. The common-circuit conclusion was conjectured by [Basso, Farhi, Marwaha, Villalonga and Zhou (2022), §7, equation (7.2)][BFMVZ]. **The finite Gaussian input.** Fix the minimiser and its diffusion, a cutoff $0[long §7, “A finite Gaussian spin and its adjacent correlations”](../long/reasoning-record.md#finite-gaussian-approximation). **Proposition 5 (circuit approximation; a consequence of [OpenAI (2026b), §§2–5][Q]).** For each fixed $T,N$ in the preceding construction with finite positive normalisers, and every $\eta>0$, there is a finite ordinary QAOA word $W$, with deterministic angles independent of $n$ and $J$, such that $$ |v(W)-S_{T,N}|<\eta. $$ **Why the adjacent pairing is the energy.** We use the rooted Gaussian representation of [OpenAI (2026b), §2 and Lemma 3.1][Q], building on the spin–boson description of [Boulebnane et al. (2026)][spin-boson]. Its classical sector consists of square-integrable functions built recursively from a local Gaussian seed and child-generated Gaussian coordinates, with inner product given by expectation. For any finite list of fixed centred real child directions, their coordinates at the receiving root have a joint centred Gaussian law. For two such directions $f,g$, $$ \mathbb E[\mathsf G(f)\mathsf G(g)]=\langle f,g\rangle. $$ The directions are fixed elements of the child space, even when their values depend on the child's Gaussian coordinates. The receiving root's seed is independent of these coordinates; compatible embeddings preserve them as the recursive depth grows. The root shift $\mathsf L$ inserts a child direction into the first Gaussian chaos (the linear Gaussian part) with constant receiving-root state. Its adjoint projects onto that part and returns the child direction. The [one-pair calculation at the start of long §8](../long/reasoning-record.md#depth-one-calibration) checks this representation's energy against the finite SK circuit before the general construction in §8.1. Start with a standard normal receiving-root seed $g_0$ and recursively put $Z_{j+1}=\mathsf G(g_j)$. The orthonormal child directions give independent standard Gaussian lifts, reproducing the scalar law. The finite spin $F_N$ depends only on those lifts. Projection therefore gives the exact rooted-energy identity $$ \begin{aligned} \mathsf L^*F_N&=\sum_{j=0}^N\mathbb E[F_NZ_{j+1}]g_j,\\ \mathcal E(F_N):=\operatorname{Re}\langle F_N,\mathsf L F_N\rangle &=\sum_{j=0}^N\mathbb E[F_Ng_j]\,\mathbb E[F_NZ_{j+1}] =S_{T,N}. \end{aligned} \tag{12} $$ Independence of the receiving-root seed removes the $j=0$ term. This identity concerns the finite Gaussian formula in a limiting rooted space, not a finite-$n$ circuit. The unshifted pairing can have the same scalar limit without identifying this energy. The construction and projection are proved in [long §8.1](../long/reasoning-record.md#rooted-energy). The shift records the lift from a child direction $g_j$ to the receiving coordinate $Z_{j+1}$. A one-step example distinguishes it from the unshifted pairing. For the nonminimising heat coefficient $\gamma=0$, take $T=4/5$ and $N=1$. Then $g_1=Z_1$ and $F_1=\operatorname{sgn}(2Z_1+Z_2)$, so Gaussian regression gives $$ S_{T,1}=\frac4{5\pi},\qquad \mathbb E[F_1g_1]\,\mathbb E[F_1Z_1]=\frac8{5\pi}. $$ This tests the finite representation, not the minimiser-dependent limit in (11). The calculation is in [long §10.4, “An exact one-step calculation”](../long/reasoning-record.md#one-step-example). **Construction underlying Proposition 5.** [OpenAI (2026b), §§3–5][Q] smooths the spin and approximates every transmitted function by a bounded smooth map, preserving oddness; smoothing the final sign alone is insufficient. Its class exclusions prevent return through a traversed branch and reserve helper classes on which the output is zero, with positive probabilities fixed during synthesis. The resulting finite formula is approximated in energy using temporary Gaussian controls, with the same sitewise seeds throughout the word. Removing those controls produces an ordinary word, whose limiting energy is $v(W)$ by the fixed-word transfer. The approximation errors are absolute and can be chosen successively for each fixed $S_{T,N}$, before it is chosen close to $P_*$. The preserved quantity is energy; the measured-configuration conclusion below uses a further concentration theorem. The complete error bound is in [long §8.6, finite-formula energy approximation](../long/reasoning-record.md#finite-formula-energy-error), with the constructions and their hypotheses in [long §§8.1–8.6](../long/reasoning-record.md#qaoa-construction). The deduction of near-optimality is now explicit: $$ P_*-v(W)\leq (P_*-I_T)+|I_T-S_{T,N}|+|S_{T,N}-v(W)|. \tag{13} $$ Choose $T$ so that $1-T<\varepsilon/3$, then $N$ so that the second term is below $\varepsilon/3$, and finally use Proposition 5 with $\eta<\varepsilon/3$. These finite choices give $v(W)>P_*-\varepsilon$ before $n$ tends to infinity. The source's Appendix A supplies an alternative positive-temperature input to the same synthesis. This construction supplies no bounds on depth or cost-angle magnitudes in terms of accuracy, and no efficient procedure for finding angles. A separate estimate for the expected energy of a specified word is described in [long §11.5](../long/reasoning-record.md#finite-size-comparison). Its threshold depends on the word's depth and cost angles. Without bounds on those parameters it gives no threshold in optimisation accuracy alone; it also supplies no rate for measurement concentration. **Corollary 6 (a measured configuration on the same instance).** For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a finite ordinary QAOA word $W_\varepsilon$, chosen independently of $n$ and $J$, such that one computational-basis measurement $\Sigma$ satisfies $$ \Pr_{J,\Sigma}\!\left\{ \max_\sigma H_{n,J}(\sigma)-H_{n,J}(\Sigma)\leq\varepsilon n \right\}\longrightarrow1 \qquad(n\to\infty). \tag{14} $$ **Proof.** For a fixed word, put $Y_n=H_{n,J}(\Sigma)/n$ and $K_n=\max_\sigma H_{n,J}(\sigma)/n$. [Farhi, Goldstone, Gutmann and Zhou, §4, equations (13)–(22)][FGGZ] prove $$ \mathbb E_{J,\Sigma}Y_n\to v(W),\qquad \mathbb E_{J,\Sigma}Y_n^2\to v(W)^2. $$ The second moment is $\mathbb E_J\langle(C_{n,J}/n)^2\rangle$, so it includes measurement variance as well as disorder fluctuations. Thus $Y_n\to v(W)$ in joint $L^2$. Gaussian concentration of the maximum and its defining mean limit give $K_n\to P_*$ in probability. Choose $W$ with $P_*-v(W)<\varepsilon/3$. With probability tending to one, both $K_n-P_*<\varepsilon/3$ and $v(W)-Y_n<\varepsilon/3$, which proves (14). The two energies use the same $J$; no independence between them is needed. The companion's [§11.2, “What is averaged, and a fixed-word probability consequence”](../long/reasoning-record.md#fixed-word-probability) gives the concentration argument and its further probability consequences.
